A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ES fine-tuning study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original Countdown, conciseness, math-reasoning, Sudoku, and ARC-AGI experiments, including performance measurements and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds GSM8K hyperparameter ablations and repeated-run Countdown results in Appendices A.2 and A.4.

M1.justification: The Gaussian perturbations, reward normalization, parameter updates, seed replay, and greedy decoding are unchanged. Algorithm 2 moves from v2 Appendix A.1 into the main text; the suggested ES/RL combination remains future work.

E1.justification: v3 newly uses GSM8K for training and evaluating hyperparameter ablations on Qwen2.5-1.5B and Qwen2.5-3B. This extends the existing mathematical-reasoning coverage; the earlier datasets and tasks are retained.

E2.justification: Countdown retains PPO-z, both GRPO-z group sizes, GRPO-v, and Dr.GRPO-v. The conciseness and math comparisons retain their original comparators, including SimpleRL-Zero, OpenReasoner-Zero, and Oat-Zero. New Table 11 repeats comparisons with existing GRPO variants without replacing the original comparisons.

E3.justification: The new GSM8K ablations use 512 fixed training prompts, 300 training steps, a 512-token generation limit, and greedy pass@1 evaluation, with population-size and noise/learning-rate sweeps. The explicitly documented settings of the retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 adds systematic ES sensitivity studies covering population size, noise scale, and learning rate across two model sizes. Appendix A.4 adds a Countdown stability analysis. These substantially expand direct testing of ES robustness beyond the retained conciseness sweeps and parameter-shift analyses.

E5.justification: v3 extends uncertainty reporting to two Countdown models through three independent seeded runs, mean and standard deviation reporting, and Student's t-tests reporting p < 0.05. This is a targeted addition; the existing four-run conciseness statistics are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 7–10 add GSM8K ablation scores, and Table 11 adds Countdown aggregates: for Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, ES reports 58.67 ± 1.47 versus Dr.GRPO-v's 44.43 ± 1.89. These supplement the unchanged original results in Tables 1–3 and Figure 2; they are not corrections to the earlier point estimates.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.8 derives approximate per-sample computational costs of 2PL FLOPs for ES and 8PL for GRPO from assumed forward and backward pass costs. This adds limited mathematical cost reasoning; the existing optimization equations and reward definitions are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the claims of billion-parameter ES optimization without dimensionality reduction, stronger Countdown performance, robustness, reduced reward hacking, and competitive math performance. The added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new ablations as supporting hyperparameter robustness and population size 30 as a performance–cost tradeoff. Its new Future Work paragraph also recognizes complementary roles for ES global exploration and gradient-based RL local refinement, adding nuance to their relationship.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 newly documents reward-hacking detection through an order-of-magnitude KL-divergence increase followed by response inspection; this clarifies the existing experiment. v3 also supplies the new ablation settings and changes the stated code-repository location from es-fine-tuning-paper to es-at-scale.

R1.justification: v3 adds Gan and Isola (2026) and Narayanan et al. (2021) for computational-cost estimation. The ARC-AGI appendix revises its discussion of Ranke (2025), replacing the account of GRPO reranking existing candidates with an explanation emphasizing the large action space. The broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v3 separates Future Work from Discussion, moves the detailed algorithm into the main text, and makes localized explanatory and wording edits. Conference information, acknowledgments, and cross-references are updated, while most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds five tables for ablations and Countdown statistics, relocates Algorithm 2, and adjusts table sizing and page flow. The original figures retain their plotted content; their relocation, including Figure 7 onto a separate page, does not represent new results.

improvement.justification: The GSM8K sensitivity studies and repeated-run Countdown statistics provide stronger support for robustness claims that v2 supported less directly. Documenting reward-hacking detection also improves transparency. The gains are incremental: the new empirical checks cover two Qwen model sizes, the FLOPs comparison is an analytical estimate, and the central method and original benchmark results remain unchanged.
